coordination.overlap: The prior E1 already identified openat2 as the stronger hostile-directory/race model while explicitly leaving it outside WP1111 unless concurrent mutation is in scope.

observed: openat2 resolves relative paths against dirfd and exposes resolve restrictions over all path components.
RESOLVE_BENEATH rejects resolution outside dirfd; RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS rejects symlink resolution in all components; RESOLVE_NO_XDEV rejects mount-point and bind-mount traversal.
With RESOLVE_BENEATH/IN_ROOT the kernel can return EAGAIN when it cannot prove that '..' did not escape because of a race or potential attack, and EXDEV when escape is detected.
openat2 is Linux-specific, present since Linux 5.6, and glibc provides no wrapper, so direct syscall use is required by the documented C interface.
The kernel documents openat2 resolution flags as protection against race conditions and attacks involving changing path components.
LOOKUP_BENEATH/LOOKUP_IN_ROOT use rename_lock and mount_lock to detect attacks affecting '..' resolution; LOOKUP_NO_XDEV blocks vfsmount traversal.
Normal path resolution follows intermediate symlinks and traverses mount points unless restricted; openat2 provides explicit all-component symlink and mount restrictions.

f2_source_observation.mechanism: _link_free_regular_file lexically rejects absolute/dot/dotdot paths and Path.is_symlink() components, then calls resolve(strict=True), verifies relative_to(root), verifies regular-file type, and later reads the returned pathname.
f2_source_observation.evidence_boundary: This is a source/static-completeness predicate. It does not claim hostile concurrent-directory mutation resistance or target-host runtime authority.

hypothesis: If the release directory can be modified concurrently by an attacker between the lexical component checks and subsequent resolve/read, the pathname-based WP1111 predicate has a check/use race class that descriptor-based kernel-enforced resolution is designed to address.
counterhypothesis: WP1111 evaluates a frozen/static release tree under repository/CI evidence scope; hostile concurrent mutation is outside its declared contract, so importing a Linux-only openat2 syscall path would add portability and maintenance cost without improving the claim WP1111 is authorized to make.

assessment.recommended_spec_clarification: Make the frozen/non-hostile-concurrent-mutation precondition explicit for WP1111. If later installer/host verification consumes attacker-writable or concurrently mutable package trees, create a separate platform-capability gate for race-safe descriptor-based resolution rather than silently upgrading this static predicate.

falsifier.for_current_no_delta_decision: Show that WP1111 is intended to authenticate or consume files from a concurrently attacker-writable release tree on the real host, or demonstrate an accepted WP1111 threat model requiring race resistance. That would invalidate the current no-openat2 decision.
falsifier.for_openat2_need: If the actual host verification boundary first snapshots or otherwise immutably pins the artifact/tree before any path validation/read, the openat2 race-hardening benefit may be redundant at that boundary.

next_exact_action: Trigger4 should keep WP1111 scoped to a frozen/static tree and, when defining the real-host package-ingest verifier, explicitly decide whether the input tree can be attacker-writable/concurrently mutable. Only that boundary should trigger an openat2/dirfd E2/E4 security design lane.
